Keep them calm, warm, and transport them safely:
Gently place the cat in a cardboard carrier lined with a soft blanket. Keep the box in a dark, quiet room.
Contact an emergency veterinary hospital or local cat rescue immediately. They have the specialized tools to help.
Do not give food, water, or medication (especially human pain relievers, which are toxic to cats) as it complicates anesthesia or treatment.
Neonate kittens (under 4 weeks) are extremely fragile:
Observe from a distance (at least 20 feet away) for 2 to 4 hours. The mother cat is their best chance at survival and might just be hunting.
If she doesn\'t return, keep them warm! Use a heating pad wrapped in towels or a warm-water bottle. Never let kittens get cold.
Standard milk will cause fatal digestive issues. Feed only warm Kitten Milk Replacer (KMR) with a needleless syringe or small bottle.
Very young kittens cannot relieve themselves. Use a warm, damp cotton ball to gently stroke their lower abdomen after feeding.
Socialization and balanced nutrition are key for kittens 4-12 weeks:
Set up a warm, quiet, enclosed space (like a bathroom) with a tiny litter box, fresh water, and high-protein kitten food.
Sit quietly near them. Offer tasty wet food on a spoon or finger. Play gently with ribbon toys to show humans are safe and fun.
Schedule a veterinary checkup for vital deworming, initial vaccinations, and professional flea treatments.
At 8-12 weeks, kittens are old enough to be spayed/neutered and adopted out. Reach out to local shelters for foster support.
For a mature kitty, we want to rule out lost pets and support community cats:
If they are friendly enough to be handled, safely secure them and take them to any local vet clinic or shelter to scan for a chip free of charge.
Snap clear photos and post on neighborhood forums (Nextdoor, Facebook Pet Groups). Hang flyers to reunite them with potential owners.
If the cat is terrified or aggressive (feral), they likely live outdoors. Research a local Trap-Neuter-Return (TNR) program to prevent breeding.
Set up a simple dry-feeding station and an insulated, weather-proof outdoor shelter to keep them comfortable in cold or rainy seasons.
Never place yourself in danger of scratches or bites.
Keep them sustained while seeking help.
They can check for microchips and lost reports.

Explore the transmission vectors, symptom recognition, and preventative care guidelines with our visual details (represented with specific supportive icons).
A fatal viral disease affecting the central nervous system.
Spreads primarily through deep saliva transfers, such as a bite or heavy scratch from an infected carrier animal (like unvaccinated strays).
Extreme behavior shifts (sudden aggression or fear), excessive salivation, jaw paralysis, and coordination failure.
Mandatory annual vaccination is 100% preventive. If scratched/bitten, wash immediately with soap under running water and seek human post-exposure vaccines.
A systemic infection caused by a microscopic protozoan parasite.
Cats contract it by hunting infected rodents or eating raw meat. Humans contract it via contact with infected feline feces (litter boxes).
Often completely silent. Symptomatic cats exhibit lethargy, high fever, breathing struggles, or eye inflammation.
Keep cats indoors to prevent hunting; feed cooked food. Pregnant women must avoid cleaning litter boxes entirely or wear gloves and scoop daily.
A bacterial infection caused by Bartonella henselae.
Transmitted among cats by fleas. Spreads to humans via a scratch or bite contaminated with flea dirt carried on claws.
Cats show no outward symptoms. In humans, a tiny red papule appears at scratch site, followed by painful swelling of lymph nodes.
Use strict vet-approved monthly flea preventatives. Avoid rough play. Wash scratches immediately with antibacterial soap.
A highly contagious skin and claw fungal infection (not a worm!).
Spreads via direct skin contact with infected animals, or touching contaminated blankets, brushes, or soil with fungal spores.
Circular patches of hair loss (alopecia), red scaly skin, dandruff, and fragile fur. Highly itchy.
Quarantine infected pets immediately. Apply topical anti-fungal treatments. Wash bedding weekly in hot bleach water.
A rapid bacterial infection found naturally in feline saliva.
Spreads immediately via deep punctures from cat bites, where oral bacteria are forced deep into muscle tissues.
Extreme throbbing pain, severe swelling, heat, and redness at the bite site within just 2 to 12 hours.
Every cat bite is a medical emergency! Seek immediate human medical care for preventative antibiotics.
Adopting an outdoor stray cat is a heartwarming, progressive process. Each stage contains visual indices and key milestones to guide you.
Observe the stray cat\'s body language and level of socialization.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_1_bullets
string-array.item: Observe from a distance to see if they are feral or simply friendly lost pets.
Provide meals at consistent times daily to build localized feeding habits.
Never force physical touch; let Lily\'s friendly knuckle greeting allow them to sniff you first.

resources.string: Seek formal vet confirmation on health status before any home introduction.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_2_bullets
string-array.item: Scan for microchips in case they are lost companions belonging to someone else.
Test for critical viruses such as FIV (Feline Immunodeficiency Virus) and FeLV (Feline Leukemia).
Administer standard flea, tick, and deworming treatments.

resources.string: Establish a dedicated, secure isolation space to prevent contamination or panic.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_3_bullets
string-array.item: Prepare a quiet room (like a bathroom) with a warm bed, clean non-clumping litter, food, and water.
Allow them to decompress in this tiny sanctuary room for at least 7 to 10 days.
Visit them regularly to speak softly and feed high-value treats to create positive bonding associations.

resources.string: Introduce scents safely under the closed door without visual tension.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_4_bullets
string-array.item: Rub a clean towel on the new cat and place it near your resident cat\'s feeding zone.
Swap toys, scratching posts, and bedding between the rooms.
Feed both cats on opposite sides of the closed isolation door to link their scents with food joy.

resources.string: Allow gradual, monitored visual sessions with a protective barrier.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_5_bullets
string-array.item: Crack the door open slightly with a secure door stopper or mesh screen.
Conduct short, 5-minute visual sessions while praising both cats with treats.
If hissed at or flattened ears occur, calmly retreat a step back and try again tomorrow.

resources.string: Commit to a lifetime of veterinary wellness, quality food, and unconditional love.

string-array.name: adopt_stage_6_bullets
string-array.item: Schedule a spay or neuter surgery to stabilize hormones and prevent stray population growth.
Provide vertical spaces, climbing shelves, and scratchers to avoid indoor territorial anxiety.
Give endless warm blankets, annual vaccinations, and the soft assurance of a permanent safe home.

CRITICAL: What NOT to feed a Cat!
A cat\'s liver and blood cells cannot process human foods. Avoid these highly toxic items entirely (represented as visual danger slots):
Destroys feline red blood cells, causing fatal hemolytic anemia.
Contains stimulants that trigger fatal muscle tremors, heart attacks, and seizures.
Causes acute, sudden kidney failure in both cats and dogs.
Causes intense intestinal pain, bloating, and severe diarrhea because adult cats lack lactase.
Swells inside the stomach, releasing toxic ethanol that causes alcohol poisoning.
A single tablespoon causes fatal brain failure and respiratory depression.
Never grab a hissing, growling, or shaking cat. Allow them space.
Sit low, avoid eye contact, and stretch your hand out slowly to let them smell you.
Place stinky wet food inside a secure humane carrier to lead them to safety.
Friendly strays might be lost pets. Take them to any vet clinic to scan their chip free.
If the cat is fearful and unsocialized, respect their home range and schedule spay/neuter surgery via TNR.

string-array.name: recipe_1_materials
string-array.item: 🐟 Salmon (100g)
🥕 Carrot slice
🍵 Warm Water

string-array.name: recipe_1_steps
string-array.item: Wash and prepare 100g of fresh boneless salmon filet.
Rinse a sweet carrot and cut a single thick slice.
Bring water to a gentle boil in a small steaming pot.
Steam the salmon filet in the pot until fully cooked and flaky.
Boil the carrot slice in water until it is very soft.
Transfer the steamed salmon to a clean cooling board.
Use two forks to flake the salmon and inspect for bones.
Mash the carrot slice with a fork into a smooth orange puree.
Blend the flaked salmon, carrot puree, and 2 tablespoons of warm water together.
Verify the meal is at room temperature and serve to your kitten.

string-array.name: recipe_2_steps
string-array.item: Acquire 100g of lean skinless chicken breast filet.
Measure 1 tablespoon of fresh pumpkin flesh.
Place the chicken breast into a pot of clean water.
Boil the chicken breast on medium heat until fully cooked.
Simmer the pumpkin pieces in boiling water until extremely soft.
Remove the chicken, let it cool, and shred into fine threads.
Mash the soft pumpkin into a velvety orange paste.
Mix the shredded chicken and pumpkin paste in a bowl.
Add 2 spoonfuls of the plain chicken cooking broth for moisture.
Stir thoroughly, let it cool, and serve this comforting stew.

string-array.name: recipe_3_steps

string-array.name: recipe_4_steps
string-array.item: Acquire one fresh organic egg and 50g of sweet potato.
Peel the sweet potato and cut it into small cubes.
Hard-boil the egg in a pot of water for 10 minutes.
Boil the sweet potato cubes until they are fully soft.
Peel the boiled egg and separate the rich yellow yolk.
Discard the egg white entirely (keep only the yellow yolk).
Mash the sweet potato cubes into a smooth, creamy paste.
Combine the egg yolk and mashed sweet potato in a bowl.
Stir in one teaspoon of warm water for a fluffy texture.
Verify the temperature is completely cool and serve.
